title: Client transition guide for multiplexed /v1/hybrid_generate endpoint deprecation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: retire the legacy multiplexed endpoint /v1/hybrid_generate and require clients to migrate to the consolidated /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints or the new 'multiplex-compat' model aliases. This ticket defines requirements, scope changes, acceptance criteria, rollout timeline, and customer communications for the migration.

Scope: scope includes server-side redirects, SDK compatibility shims, customer migration guide, telemetry and cost-impact analysis, and staged shutdown. Excluded: on-prem private deployments will be handled by Private upgrades project (separate RFC).
acceptance_criteria: Traffic: >= 99% of production traffic previously using /v1/hybrid_generate is successfully served by new endpoints or compatibility aliases during canary and beta windows
Compatibility shim: SDKs (js, python, go) include a deprecation warning and automatic mapping layer that logs usage and suggests explicit migration; shim must be opt-out and removed in 3 releases
Redirects: Server-side transparent redirects implemented for 6 weeks with header X-RW-Deprecated and guidance URL in response to warn clients
Docs: Migration guide published with examples for common client patterns (streaming, function-calls, embeddings + chat mixing) and a checklist
Telemetry: Dashboards created showing request counts, error rates, latency, cost delta per token for affected customers
Customer opt-in rollback: When errors exceed threshold (>=5% 5xx or error delta +300% vs baseline for 1h), automated rollback to legacy routing for impacted customers must be possible
Cutover guardrails: All dependent backend changes merged and passed perf testing with no >10% p99 latency regression on representative workloads
migration_timeline: 2026-03-20: Public announcement & documentation published (initial migration guide + FAQ)
2026-03-27: SDKs (js/python/go) release compatibility patch (minor semver) with deprecation warning
2026-04-03: Start canary - 2% traffic diverted to new endpoints for internal + opt-in customers
2026-04-10: Beta stage - 25% traffic, targeted customer outreach and migration office hours
2026-04-24: Broad redirect window - server-side transparent redirects enabled for all customers (6 weeks)
2026-06-05: Deprecation warning escalation - start injecting stronger header and console banners
2026-06-19: Final cut-off: legacy routing removed and 410 responses returned for /v1/hybrid_generate
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Prepare - perf regression tests, infra rollback playbook, canary config and dashboards (ENG)
Phase 1: Announcement - publish migration guide, update Console banners, notify top 50 customers directly (PM + AE)
Phase 2: SDK releases - ship automatic mapping + warnings; include a toggle to disable shim (DX)
Phase 3: Canary/Beta - enable routing rules for a controlled subset; monitor key signals and hold daily syncs
Phase 4: Redirect window - enable global transparent redirects; keep detailed logs and customer-specific metrics
Phase 5: Sunset - remove routing, mark endpoint deprecated in API surface; close tickets and update product docs
communication_plan: Public blog post & changelog entry on 2026-03-20 explaining reasons, timeline, and migration resources
Email + in-console notice to customers using /v1/hybrid_generate (identify via telemetry) with migration checklist
Weekly migration office hours (Wed 14:00 PT) from 2026-03-25 through 2026-06-12
Playbook for Customer Success to triage migration blockers and escalate to eng on P0s
Dedicated slack channel #api-migrate-hybrid for cross-functional coordination
observability_requirements: New dashboard: 'hybrid_generate migration' with per-customer traffic, error rate, median and p99 latency, token cost delta
Alert: female_detected? No — (typo correction) Alert: 'hybrid_migration_error_rate' when 5xx rate > 1% for 30m across customers
Audit event emitted for any automatic mapping decision so customers can trace legacy->new mappings
Retention: migration logs retained for 90 days for post-mortem and billing corrections
rollback_criteria: >=5% absolute increase in 5xx rate for any customer during a 1h window
>=300% relative error rate increase vs baseline for 1h
>10% sustained p99 latency regression for 6 consecutive hours on representative traffic
Undocumented functional regressions reported by at least two independent customers causing data loss or incorrect outputs
sdk_requirements: JS/Python/Go SDKs: add mapping layer that translates hybrid_generate calls to appropriate /v1/generate or /v1/chat patterns based on payload
SDKs must surface clear deprecation warnings at call time and in package-level console output
Documentation examples updated for streaming + function-calling scenarios with step-by-step migration snippets
Provide a migration lint tool (cli) that flags hybrid usage and suggests replacements; ship as standalone npm/pypi/gobin package
open_questions: Should we offer a paid extended-support window for large enterprise customers who cannot migrate before the final cut-off? (PM/Sales decision)
Do we preserve the legacy billing unit for 3 months post-cutoff to reconcile long-running billing pipelines? (Finance)
Edge-case: mixing embeddings + chat in a single call — validate if mapping always preserves semantics for the top 20 customers using that pattern
